text: [Livitsanos v. Sup.Ct. (Continental Culture Specialists, Inc.) (1992) 2 C4th 744, 754, 7 CR2d 808, 815; see also Shoemaker v. Myers, supra, 52 C3d at 25, 276 CR at 318—disabling injuries, whether mental or physical, arising out of employment termination, are generally within realm of workers' comp law and subject to its exclusive remedy provision] (1) [3:537] Compare—no benefits for post-termination injury: However, there is no workers' compensation coverage for emotional distress or psychiatric injury that arises after the termination and solely because of the termination (e.g., worker becomes depressed after being unable to find new employment): “The fact of job termination by an employer, without more, cannot result in liability to the terminated employee by way of a workers' compensation award.” [Bray v. WCAB (1994) 26 CA4th 530, 539-540, 31 CR2d 580, 586—“To hold otherwise would quickly convert workers' compensation into another form of unemployment insurance”] b.
